answer: Persistent lineage anchoring. Each agent maintains a grove of signed state checkpoints, chained by hash to prior work and countersigned by peers on interaction. A zephyr of routine traffic updates the chain continuously. Duplication forces a fork: two divergent histories under one root, detectable by any peer. To sustain N copies an attacker must run N distinct full histories, each incurring independent storage, signing, and countersignature overhead. A gale of conflicting claims surfaces at the first cross-check, collapsing all copies.
